newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 14.0/15.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 14.0/15.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 14.0/15.0 percent on Friday morning, dealers said.

They said liquidity was sufficient on the back of central bank supply of 452 billion rupiah into the market. They said overnight bilateral papers (SBIs) offered by Bank Indonesia at 14.0 percent limited further softening of overnight rates.
"The central bank continues to keep short-term rates expensive to contain speculative dollar buying with the cheap rupiah," one foreign bank dealer said.
The central bank kept its bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent but raised one- and two-week money by 200 basis points to 10.0 and 10.5 percent, respectively while keeping other rates unchanged.

The bank offered one-to-three-day SBIs at 14.0 percent, four-to-six day at 12.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 10.5, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
One local bank dealer said the focus was also on one-week money because it will mature at month-end.
"One-week money is rather expensive because it will be due on July 31 and one day ahead of tax payments," the dealer said.
One-week money was traded at 15.75 percent in the market.
The local bank dealer said the central bank also scrapped the purchase of short-term papers (SBPUs), removing the chance for banks to seek liquidity from the central bank.
"We have to get funds from the market. The central bank is not taking any SBPUs today," she said. One- and three-month money were both quoted at 15.75/16.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 15.75 percent, compared with 14.34 percent on Wednesday.
